summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the selected Latin. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the repentance language, assurances and negations, commandment obligations, life-and-death consequences, blood-guilt, and remedy for sins. The notes distinguish supplied elliptical wording and the contextual shepherd interpretation from explicitly expressed text, preserve the alternative interpretation of hic, and accurately disclose the supplied apparatus report without replacing the working reading faciunt. The simplified edition retains these meanings despite its shorter sentences. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of reported alternatives; it does not authenticate unseen editions, catalogue entries, manuscript handwriting, or exhaustive collation.
